content.comment_body: I'm experiencing a similar issue. Using [product_name] [version_no] on Windows 10 64-bit. I've relied on UDFs often before and find them essential. Currently, when building simple tank infill routines, following previous methods, the UDF entry remains disabled—even for basic circuits. They are saved in a dedicated folder. I verified hardware assignments match between circuit and UDF, and experimented with variations such as [product_name] udf version, yet the issue persists. My screenshot shows I’ve picked valid targets and there are no creation errors. (Split from UDF not Usable in Circuit Diagram).
Could you upload your UDF as a ZIP for review?

This behavior is expected if unfinished blocks remain in the circuit; for example, check blocks B008 and B011, which need AMx to complete the analog outputs. Once those connections are made, the circuit should function correctly. Tip: After creating a new UDF, press F2 to assign the logo, then check the info window for any errors or missing parts. Regards, [user_name]
There are additional issues beyond just the missing analog flags—two analog inputs (AI2 and AI3) in the UDF aren't connected within the function itself.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that the UDF (User Defined Function) in [product_name] [version_no] may show up as unavailable in the interface, usually due to incomplete blocks or missing connections inside the UDF. This often involves analog outputs or inputs not being properly configured. UDFs are critical for building modular, reusable logic and such errors can disrupt normal workflow.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect error-free UDFs to be immediately selectable and usable within logic circuits, based on prior experience. Clear error messaging or guidance is anticipated when configuration problems prevent UDF selection.
